extra_info: El Capitan is a granite rock formation in Yosemite National Park. It rises about 3,000 feet (900 meters) above Yosemite Valley.
task_instruction: Rewrite each direct wh-question as a reported question.
paragraphs: A journalist interviews climber Alex Honnold about his 2017 free solo ascent of El Capitan. The journalist begins by asking about his preparation. The journalist asked Alex, {{red:When did you first decide to attempt the climb?}} {{mask_1}} Alex described how the idea developed over time. The journalist asked, {{red:How long had you been preparing for that route?}} {{mask_2}} Alex explained that he had spent years climbing and studying the route.

They discuss the scale of the wall and the route known as Freerider. The journalist asked Alex, {{red:Which section required the most careful planning?}} {{mask_3}} Alex described the sections that demanded close attention. The journalist asked, {{red:What made the route especially challenging?}} {{mask_4}} Alex talked about its length and technical difficulty. The journalist asked, {{red:How did you remember the sequence of moves?}} {{mask_5}} Alex explained that repeated practice helped him learn it.

The journalist asks about the term free solo. Alex clarifies that it means climbing without a rope or protective equipment, making the activity exceptionally dangerous. The journalist asked, {{red:Why did you choose to climb without a rope?}} {{mask_6}} Alex explained his personal reasons without presenting them as advice. The journalist asked, {{red:What risks did you consider before the ascent?}} {{mask_7}} Alex said that a fall could have fatal consequences. The journalist asked, {{red:How did you decide whether the conditions were suitable?}} {{mask_8}} Alex described assessing the conditions and his own readiness.

They talk about concentration during a long climb. The journalist asked Alex, {{red:Where did you focus your attention on the wall?}} {{mask_9}} Alex described concentrating on the next section of the route. The journalist asked, {{red:What did you do when you reached a difficult sequence?}} {{mask_10}} Alex explained how he managed his attention. The journalist asked, {{red:How often had you practiced those movements before the climb?}} {{mask_11}} Alex said that he had repeated them many times while preparing. The journalist asked, {{red:Who supported you during the planning process?}} {{mask_12}} Alex spoke about the people who had helped him prepare.

The interview turns to how the public responded. The journalist asked Alex, {{red:What questions did viewers ask after the climb?}} {{mask_13}} Alex said many people had asked about the preparation and the risks. The journalist asked, {{red:How did the experience change your view of climbing?}} {{mask_14}} Alex reflected on how the ascent had affected him. The journalist asked, {{red:Which part of the media coverage surprised you most?}} {{mask_15}} Alex described one unexpected reaction. The journalist asked, {{red:What would you tell someone who is curious about climbing?}} {{mask_16}} Alex encouraged people to learn from qualified instructors and to use appropriate safety equipment.

Before the interview ends, the journalist asks what Alex hopes viewers will understand. The journalist asked, {{red:Why is it important to distinguish a professional's experience from general safety advice?}} {{mask_17}} Alex said that individual experience should not be treated as a safe method for others. The journalist asked, {{red:Where can beginners learn about climbing safely?}} {{mask_18}} Alex recommended seeking instruction from qualified professionals. The journalist asked, {{red:What should people consider before choosing a climbing activity?}} {{mask_19}} Alex said they should consider training, conditions, and appropriate protection. Finally, the journalist asked, {{red:How do you hope people will remember the ascent?}} {{mask_20}} Alex said he hoped they would remember both the achievement and the importance of understanding its risks.
